summary: G. V. Aston specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy from the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under doctoral supervisor B. Jack Copeland and teacher Paul Harrison.

G. V. Devasthali (1906–1993) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (attested 1944) and as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin M. Nagao (1907–2005) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hadani and Susumu Yamaguchi, he held Kyoto University's Chair of Buddhist Studies (1935–1971) and taught at Kyushu University and Tekko Junior College.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule (b. 1920) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

Galsan Gomboev (1818–1863) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Józef Kowalewski. He taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington. Working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and other fields, he taught at the University of Ceylon, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He served as department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Calcutta.

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, and Allahabad, he was Professor of Sanskrit at Muir Central College, Principal of Sanskrit College and University, and Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

Gangs zhun is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Qinghai Nationalities Normal College and earned a master's degree from Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under MA supervisor Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MPhil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche (b. 1967) is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Jean Daniel Kieffer, and held a chair in Indian languages at INALCO from approximately 1828 to 1878.

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (ended 2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham (b. 1948) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, he was Lecturer in Tibetan Language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb (b. 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011, 2026).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Goh Wee Kian specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisor Hui-Chieh Loy, foster supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder (b. 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and other fields. He studied at Reed College, UC Berkeley, and with traditional teachers Isshu Miura and Sesso Oda, later serving as professor at the University of California, Davis from 1986.
